ai.description: Naja kaouthia reaches 1.2–1.5 meters. It is typically brown, gray, or black with a distinct O-shaped, white-bordered hood mark. A dark ventral band is often present across the throat.
ai.identificationRemarks: The most reliable diagnostic feature of *Naja kaouthia* is the distinct, complete O-shaped (monocle) pattern on the rear of its hood, unlike the binocellate mark of *N. naja*.
ai.habitat: *Naja kaouthia* inhabits diverse lowland environments, including rice paddies, marshes, and grasslands, typically occurring from sea level up to 1,000 meters in elevation.
ai.behavior: The monocled cobra is primarily crepuscular and terrestrial, often foraging for rodents and frogs in rice paddies and wetlands during the twilight hours.
ai.reproductionNotes: Naja kaouthia is oviparous, breeding primarily from January to April. Females lay clutches of 10–30 eggs in burrows or mounds, which they guard until hatching.
ai.distributionRemarks: The Monocled Cobra inhabits the northeastern states of India, West Bengal, and Odisha, ranging from sea level up to 1,000 meters in tropical and subtropical zones.
